status_note: Reproduces on Snowflake 10.40.102. The docs give `NUMBER` a precision of at most 38 digits (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/data-types-numeric), and `NUMBER(39,0)` is a compile error, but arithmetic results, and casts of them, hold values to 2^127 with 39 digits. Not searched in Snowflake's community forum yet.
summary: Arithmetic on `NUMBER(38,0)` returns values past 38 digits without an error: `10^38 - 1 + 1` is `10^38`, typed `NUMBER(38,0)`, and a cast of it to `NUMBER(38,0)` succeeds. Only results past 128 bits (2^127) raise. A column of a declared precision can so hold a value it cannot represent, and the error that should come at 38 digits comes later or not at all.
handling: sverify's SQL checks every integer result against the 64-bit range, far inside 38 digits, and does not write decimals for Snowflake yet (#27). When it does, each result needs a check against its declared precision.
